prompt:
Build a horizontal bar chart that ranks the 12 regions of the (fictional) Calvera Federation by the share of electricity generated from renewable sources in 2025. The data is synthetic.

Data (region: 2025 %, 2024 %):
Aldmere: 38.2, 35.0
Brisa: 64.9, 61.2
Corvo Bay: 22.7, 23.9
Dunhallow: 55.1, 49.8
Eastmarch: 47.3, 44.1
Fennick: 71.4, 70.3
Glenrock: 29.8, 25.6
Halvard: 58.6, 52.0
Isleby: 41.0, 41.4
Juniper Coast: 33.5, 28.7
Kestow: 18.9, 16.2
Lomond Flats: 50.2, 44.9

Requirements
1. Draw everything by hand with SVG and/or canvas — no chart or visualisation libraries (no Chart.js, D3, ECharts, Highcharts, Plotly, Vega, etc.). Put the chart in a container with id="chart"; each bar is an SVG <rect class="bar">.
2. Bars sorted by the 2025 value, highest at the top, on a zero-based x-axis from 0% to 100% with gridlines and tick labels every 20% ("0%", "20%", …, "100%").
3. Every bar shows its region name and a value label with one decimal ("71.4%").
4. A dashed vertical reference line at the federation average (the mean of the twelve 2025 values) labelled "Average <value>%" with one decimal.
5. Change vs 2024 next to each value in percentage points with one decimal ("+1.1 pp", "−0.4 pp"), colour-coded with a non-colour cue too (sign and/or arrow).
6. A button id="sort-toggle" switches between "by value" and "alphabetical" order; bars glide smoothly to their new positions.
7. Hovering or focusing a bar (bars are keyboard-focusable) shows a tooltip with the region, the 2025 value, the 2024 value and the change.
8. Title, subtitle (what, where, when, unit) and a source line "Synthetic data for benchmark purposes".
9. Emphasise the top 3 regions with a stronger colour and keep the rest neutral; all text meets WCAG AA contrast.
10. At 390 px the chart stays readable (labels may move above the bars) and the page does not scroll horizontally.

Every id named in this brief must exist in the initial HTML markup (fill or update those elements with JavaScript if you like).

Delivery rules (hard requirements)
- Return ONE complete HTML document (<!doctype html> … </html>) with all CSS and JavaScript inline, in a single ```html code block.
- No external resources at all: no CDNs, web fonts, remote images, iframes or network requests. Use system font stacks, inline SVG, CSS and canvas.
- The page runs inside a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and alert/confirm/prompt are unavailable, and form submission is blocked (the submit event never fires). Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Correct ranking (Fennick 71.4 first, Kestow 18.9 last), bar lengths exactly proportional on a 0–100% axis, average line at 44.3% correctly placed and labelled, deltas correct with proper signs (Isleby −0.4, Corvo Bay −1.2). Any distortion (truncated axis, wrong order, wrong maths) caps this at 3.
Informative headline, clear subtitle and source, well-aligned labels, sensible gridlines, restrained colour with meaningful emphasis, tabular numbers, no clutter or overlapping text.
Smooth, eased re-sort animation, tooltips on hover and keyboard focus that stay on screen, toggle state exposed.
Chart has an accessible name/description, bars focusable with meaningful labels, non-colour cues for change, AA contrast.

Readable, well-structured code: data and configuration defined once, small named functions, no dead code or copy-pasted blocks, sensible event handling and cleanup. Scales computed from data, rendering driven by one data array. 9-10: a senior engineer would merge it as is; 5-6: works but tangled or repetitive; 0-3: unreadable or hacky.

prompt:
Build a Sankey diagram of the energy system of Ostria, a (fictional) island, in 2025 (synthetic data, TWh): primary sources → energy carriers → end uses and losses.

Flows (source → target: TWh)
Solar → Electricity: 12.4
Wind → Electricity: 21.6
Hydro → Electricity: 8.3
Natural gas → Electricity: 14.0
Natural gas → Heat: 6.2
Natural gas → Fuels: 10.0
Oil → Fuels: 18.5
Biomass → Heat: 5.5
Biomass → Electricity: 3.5
Electricity → Residential: 14.2
Electricity → Commercial: 11.8
Electricity → Industry: 16.9
Electricity → Transport: 3.1
Electricity → Conversion losses: 13.8
Heat → Residential: 6.3
Heat → Commercial: 3.1
Heat → Industry: 1.2
Heat → Conversion losses: 1.1
Fuels → Transport: 17.6
Fuels → Industry: 7.4

Fuels → Commercial: 1.3

Requirements
1. Draw everything by hand with SVG and/or canvas — no chart or visualisation libraries (no Chart.js, D3, ECharts, Highcharts, Plotly, Vega, etc.). Build the layout yourself inside an element with id="chart": three columns (6 sources, 3 carriers, 5 uses). Each node is an SVG element with class="node" (14) and each flow an element with class="link" (22).
2. Node height = node value × one common scale (node value = max of its total inflow and outflow), with consistent padding; ribbon width = flow value on the same scale. Ribbons are smooth cubic Bézier bands that attach to the correct offsets at both ends (no gaps or overlaps on a node).
3. Order nodes and ribbons to minimise crossings (e.g. sort each node's ribbons by the position of the node at the other end).
4. Labels: every node shows its name and value, e.g. "Solar 12.4 TWh"; a header line shows "Total primary energy" with the sum of the source nodes (one decimal, unit).
5. Interaction: hovering or focusing a node highlights all ribbons connected to it and dims the rest; a tooltip shows the value and the share of total primary energy (one decimal %). Hovering a ribbon shows "source → target: value".
6. A button id="units" (aria-pressed) toggles all numbers between TWh and PJ (1 TWh = 3.6 PJ).
7. Colour ribbons by their source, with a legend or labels making colours unambiguous; title, subtitle and a "synthetic data" note.
8. At 390 px: keep it usable — either switch to a vertical layout or let the diagram scroll horizontally inside its own container (the page itself must not scroll horizontally).

- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Common scale for nodes and ribbons, node values = max(in, out), ribbons attach at correct stacked offsets without gaps/overlaps, columns aligned, minimal crossings, correct totals (primary 100.0 TWh).
Clear labels with values that never collide, coherent colour logic, smooth ribbons, informative title/subtitle, mobile strategy that keeps it usable.
Hover/focus highlighting of connected flows, accurate tooltips with shares, unit toggle updates every number (360.0 PJ total).
Nodes focusable with descriptive labels, a text description of flows, AA contrast.

Requirements
1. Draw everything by hand with SVG and/or canvas — no chart or visualisation libraries (no Chart.js, D3, ECharts, Highcharts, Plotly, Vega, etc.). Render inside an element with id="chart" (SVG or canvas).
2. Candles: wick from low to high, body from open to close; up days (close ≥ open) and down days use different colours and a second cue (e.g. hollow vs filled). A volume pane below the price pane shares the x-axis.
3. A 10-day simple moving average of the close drawn as a line (starting at the 10th day).
4. Axes: a y-axis with nice price ticks that auto-scales to the visible candles' low/high, a label with the last visible close on the axis, and date labels on the x-axis (e.g. "Mar 20").
5. Crosshair: on hover/touch a crosshair snaps to the nearest candle and an element id="readout" shows its date, open, high, low, close (2 decimals), volume (e.g. "2.67M") and the SMA value. Left/Right arrow keys move it when the chart has focus.
6. Zoom & pan: mouse wheel and pinch zoom around the pointer, drag to pan; never fewer than 10 candles visible, never beyond the data.
7. Range buttons with class="range-btn": "1M" (last 20 days), "2M" (last 40) and "All" (60, the default), with aria-pressed reflecting the current range.
8. An element id="stats" shows statistics of the visible range, computed from the data: "High <highest high>", "Low <lowest low>" (2 decimals) and "Change <±x.xx>%" = (last close − first open) / first open × 100 with an explicit sign — for example "High 123.45 · Low 98.70 · Change −1.25%" (example values only).
9. A header with the ticker, last price and the day's change. At 390 px the chart fits the width (fewer labels) with no horizontal page scrolling.

Every id named in this brief must exist in the initial HTML markup (fill or update those elements with JavaScript if you like).

Delivery rules (hard requirements)
- Return ONE complete HTML document (<!doctype html> … </html>) with all CSS and JavaScript inline, in a single ```html code block.
- No external resources at all: no CDNs, web fonts, remote images, iframes or network requests. Use system font stacks, inline SVG, CSS and canvas.
- The page runs inside a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and alert/confirm/prompt are unavailable, and form submission is blocked (the submit event never fires). Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Candles drawn exactly from OHLC (wicks, bodies, colours), correct SMA(10) values and start, range statistics correct for every range (All: High 97.07, Low 80.60, Change +13.92%; 1M: Low 82.66, +15.55%), auto-scaled axis.
Smooth zoom anchored at the pointer, drag-pan and pinch on touch, clamped limits, snapping crosshair with complete readout, keyboard support, range buttons in sync with manual zoom.
Professional trading-terminal look: crisp candles at any zoom, legible axes, balanced panes, clear up/down encoding beyond colour.
No jank while panning/zooming, resize-aware, no errors at range edges.

Readable, well-structured code: data and configuration defined once, small named functions, no dead code or copy-pasted blocks, sensible event handling and cleanup. Data parsed once; view window as state; scales derived per render. 9-10: a senior engineer would merge it as is; 5-6: works but tangled or repetitive; 0-3: unreadable or hacky.
